reason: E2 directly supports the nanocrystalline diffusion and Y pinning premises. E1 supports the premise that Mn-rich non-protective oxides form in CrMnFeCoNi, but it contradicts the hypothesis's implication that Cr2O3 or Al2O3 scales are expected in this system without the intervention, and it does not address the 700–1100 °C range or the coarse-grained baseline behavior. E3 is about V-rich oxides in TiAl alloys and is irrelevant to the key premises.
premises: Nanocrystalline microstructure enhances grain-boundary diffusion of oxide-formers (Cr, Al) to form a continuous protective scale
Trace reactive elements (Y) improve oxide scale adhesion via interfacial pinning (e.g., Y2O3 particles)
Coarse-grained alloys without reactive elements form discontinuous, non-protective oxides (e.g., Mn-rich) that degrade performance
The beneficial effects hold over a temperature range of 700–1100 °C
In CrMnFeCoNi, Mn-rich non-protective oxides form instead of Cr2O3 or Al2O3 under high-temperature oxidation
